sentences.text: This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act filed by the appellants/claimants arising out of the award dated 27.02.2015 passed by Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (hereinafter referred as "Claims Tribunal), District- Morena in Claim Case No.286/2013 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. The date of accident, negligence and issue of liability are not in dispute, however, the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard is not in question.

3. As per the findings of the Tribunal in the case of death of Kallu due to motor accident, Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.5,97,000/- with interest from the date of filing of claim application till its realization.

4. Counsel for appellants submitted that compensation as awarded by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20451 2 MA-535-2015 Claims Tribunal in assessing the income of deceased to the tune of Rs.3,000/- per month is inadequate and is on the lower side.
It is further submitted that deceased was working as manson by fitting tiles and earned Rs.10,000/- per month from the same.

Learned counsel for the claimants contended that Claims Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased and in not adding any future prospects as well as reasonable other heads i.e. loss of estate, loss of consortium, funeral expenses etc.

It is further contended by counsel for claimants that Claims Tribunal has wrongly deduced amount towards personal expenses Smt. Girja Devi vs Amit Sharma on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170679630/
1 as 1/3 as there are five dependents on the deceased.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, it is prayed that reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded to the claimants.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation and argued in support of the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal.

6. Heard the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Tribunal.
7.
After hearing counsel for the parties, it is found that Claims Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased is on lower side.

In considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper amount of the income of the deceased in the present case i s Rs.5,270/- per month of an unskilled labour instead of Rs.3,000/- per month which has wrongly been assessed by the Claims Tribunal.

8. As regards loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700 , the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects of 40%.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20451 3 MA-535-2015 and ors.

entities.text: Sarla Verma NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20451 3 MA-535-2015 and ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 , even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, Claims Tribunal has rightly applied multiplier of 18 as well as the deduction for personal expenses should have been 1/4th.
Therefore, findings recorded by Claims Tribunal in this regard is modified and 1/4th of the amount must be deduced towards personal expenses.

9. Accordingly, appellants- claimants are entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD AMOUN  Income Rs.5270/- pm  Annual Income Rs.5270 x 12= 6
after adding Future Prospects 40% Rs.88536/-

After deducting dependency 1/4 Rs.66402/-
 Multiplier (18) Rs.1195236/-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.40000x 5= 2,
 Other Heads:- Rs.30,000/-

Total Compensation = 
10.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.14,25,236/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.5,97,000/- .
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.8,28,236/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
11. In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.8,28,236/- .
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.

2 period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
